## Classes

### `class KernelBootstrap`

KernelBootstrap — the OS kernel layer. Owns: - The single shared WebGPU device (if available). - The central task scheduler (kernel-owned RAF). - The event bus. - GPU device-lost fan-out to all registered apps. - The syscall surface exposed to apps. Tier-2 note: In Tier 2 this becomes a Rust native-host service; the kernel.syscalls shape must remain stable across tiers.

| `_failNaviDependentBindings` | `_failNaviDependentBindings(state, errorCode = null)` | Mirror a terminal continuity outcome onto every dependent Navi service. `_scheduleNaviOperatorRebind` pins all dependents to `operator-rebinding` synchronously, but they are only re-bound after continuity publishes. If the rebind ends before that point, those services keep a transient state that nothing will ever resolve: the authority recovery net refuses to run while continuity is unavailable, so every later request waits out its full transient budget and then fails on a state that cannot change. Publishing the same terminal state keeps the dependents honest and lets callers fail fast with an actionable reason. This is only for outcomes with no follow-up bind. A pre-change boundary is deliberately left transient because its committing Profile event will bind the next operator. |

### `class KernelEventBus`

Minimal synchronous event bus for kernel-internal use. Apps should use kernel.syscalls.ipc for cross-app messaging.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
